AutoPrReviewEngine.AttachMentionAsync finds the covering task by the pull request\\u0027s external reference alone (AutoPrReviewEngine.cs:2067-2076). Its gates (2241-2380) never look at the assignee or owner root. TaskDecider.ClaimForMentionFollowUp (TaskDecider.cs:2280) documents that it does no owner identity check. The v0.11.3 owner-root rule (TaskOwnerRule, 5bacf6fa1/95e7e900b/baef0c975) is applied only in CLI commands, never in the daemon. The receive gate (EventReplicationInbox.EvaluateTaskActVerdict, v0.11.0) protects only the receiving ledger and always lets an Owner-role sender\\u0027s act through, so it cannot stop a teammate\\u0027s node from claiming and launching on its own machine.\\n\\nShape to weigh: apply the same TaskOwnerRule the CLI uses at the attach and claim seam. A teammate\\u0027s mention that lands on another owner\\u0027s task should be recorded (or routed to that teammate as their own item) without a claim. Decide whether the Owner-role pass-through in the receive gate should also cover daemon-originated claims on another owner\\u0027s task.\\n\\n## Motivating case: AgelessRx/arx-platform#2166, pr-review task bc7d2572 (2026-10-01 EDT)\\n\\n- bc7d2572 is Brian\\u0027s (Hallmanac) pr-review task for #2166, scope Team, assigned to Brian Hall. The comment answered Taylor; nothing in it was for Brian.\\n- 17:23 feed: \\u0022bc7d2572 claimed by TaylorDenny as a deliberate kick-off; a run is starting\\u0022. Taylor\\u0027s install had a real mention of its own login, found Brian\\u0027s replicated task by external reference with no owner filter, and claimed it through TaskDecider.ClaimForMentionFollowUp. That claim carries the empty node id, so the feed (OrchestratorFeedDescription.cs:124-125) labelled it a deliberate kick-off. That label is wrong.\\n- 17:26 feed: \\u0022bc7d2572 claimed by node ef6ab27d\\u0022.
